annotations.title: Road conditions now: closures, chains, weather

description:
Do I need chains on I-80 to Tahoe right now? Is US-50 open over Echo Summit? Caltrans chain controls, lane and ramp closures, road-weather stations and message-sign text on I-80 (San Francisco to the Nevada line), US-50 (West Sacramento to Stateline), I-15 (San Diego to Primm) and I-5 in California, each at its route mile with the nearest dog stop.
Live state, not rules: Caltrans feed data fetched every 15 minutes (fetched_at in the result), never a verified fact. For the day of a mountain or desert drive: Donner Summit, Echo Summit, Cajon Pass, the Grapevine. It reports conditions, not places to stop: each condition carries only the nearest dog stop. Nevada roads and other highways are not covered.
Inputs: route ("I-80", "80", "US 50", "Highway 50", "I-15", "I-5"); a window as from_mile and to_mile, or town (a town or named stretch on the route: Truckee, Donner Pass, South Lake Tahoe, Placerville, Cajon Pass, Barstow) with direction and ahead_miles; direction alone keeps that direction's closures, signs and chain controls. With no window, the whole route in California.
chain_controls_in_effect is true when a Caltrans chain-control point in the window reports a control (any status but R-0), with Caltrans' own wording; a sign that mentions chains is listed under signs with its text. Each weather station says whether its reading is current (the feeds sometimes carry readings months old; those numbers are left out of the text). A document older than two hours is marked stale; when no document can be read the answer has outcome unavailable and the address of Caltrans QuickMap, the live map.

Examples:
  - "Do I need chains on I-80 to Tahoe right now?" -> route="I-80", direction="east"
  - "Is Highway 50 open over Echo Summit?" -> route="Highway 50", town="Echo Summit"
  - "Closures on I-15 from Barstow to the Nevada line" -> route="I-15", town="Barstow", direction="north", ahead_miles=120

ahead_miles.description: With town: miles from it in the direction of travel (default 50), or on each side of it without a direction (default 25)

direction.description: Direction of travel. Keeps that direction's closures, signs and chain controls (and those for both ways); with town, the window runs ahead of it. North and east mean increasing route miles

from_mile.description: Start of a mile range on the route (the road-trip guide's miles)

response_format.description: 'markdown' for readable text, 'json' for structured data

to_mile.description: End of a mile range on the route

town.description: A town or named stretch on the route ("Truckee", "Donner Pass", "South Lake Tahoe", "Cajon Pass", "Barstow")

name: dogpolicies_road_conditions

accepted.description: With bad_input: each argument that could not be read, with the values it accepts

chain_controls.description: The chain-control points in the window with a control in effect

chain_controls_in_effect.description: A Caltrans chain-control point in the window reports a control in effect

chains_in_effect.description: A chain control in effect or a sign that mentions chains, counted the same way as in the I-5 conditions answer

code.description: With an outcome other than ok: not_found, invalid, unavailable

did_you_mean.description: Close matches to what was asked for: towns, places, slugs or brands, best first

feeds_failed.description: District feeds that did not answer at the last fetch

fetched_at.description: When the loop fetched the feeds; null when no document could be read

live_map.description: Caltrans QuickMap, the live map of the same feeds

nearest.description: When nothing is inside the radius: the nearest places in the data, with distance_miles

next.description: Calls that would answer the question, in words

outcome.description: Absent or ok: a normal answer. no_match: nothing in the data matches, see did_you_mean, nearest and next. bad_input: the arguments cannot be used as given, see next. partial: some of the ids were found, see missing. unavailable: a live source could not be read. None of these is an error.

resolved_from.description: Set when a word was read as the value the tool uses: hotel as lodging, NB as north. Each key is the argument; asked is what was sent, used what it was read as

route.description: Route id (i-80, us-50, i-15, i-5); null when the route is not covered

stale.description: True when the document is older than two hours

weather.description: Road-weather stations in the window; current is false when the station's reading is more than two hours older than fetched_at

title: Road conditions now: closures, chains, weather
